title: Toronto police cleared in death of Otto Vass
article: Four police officers charged in the death of a man during a fight outside a convenience store three years ago were cleared Wednesday of manslaughter charges.
Constables Phillip Duncan, Robert Lemaitre, Filippo Bevilacqua and Nam Le had each pleaded not guilty to one count each of manslaughter in the Aug. 9, 2000, death of Otto Vass.
Toronto Police Chief Julian Fantino said he was relieved about the verdict and added that the officers would return to their duties shortly.

"It's an outcome we were were all hoping for and we're glad it turned out this way," Chief Fantino said outside court. "Their families have gone through three years of hell ... at the end of the day, justice prevailed."
An Ontario court heard last month that police were called to a convenience store in the city's west end on the night of Aug. 9, 2000, after Mr. Vass had been in an earlier fight with three youths.
Mr. Vass at first appeared calm while giving police information, but then suddenly starting punching Constable Lemaitre in the head, Constable Duncan testified.

Constable Duncan also said Mr. Vass kept saying "I'm going to get you, pig" during a brief struggle in which Mr. Vass was finally subdued. He stopped breathing and efforts to revive him failed, court was told.
Constable Duncan admitted to striking Mr. Vass with the palm of his hand three or four times during the confrontation but he said he never kicked or hit the man with his baton.
The pathologist who conducted the autopsy testified that Mr. Vass died when a fat embolism broke off because of the blows from the officers and travelled to his lungs.
